title: Being integral descends along fpqc coverings (Stacks 02L9)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. For $i\in I$ let $f_i:X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ be the base change of $f$ along $g_i$, the second projection of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $f_i$ is integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] for every $i\in I$, then $f$ is integral.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L9 (lemma-descending-property-integral, line 6087: 'The property P(f) = "f is integral" is fpqc local on the base'), the direction 'each base change $X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ has the property $\Rightarrow$ $f$ has it' of 'fpqc local on the base', Descent, Definition Tag 02KO (definition-property-morphisms-local, line 5310)

proof.text: *Step 1 (each $f_i$ is affine and universally closed).* Fix $i\in I$. By hypothesis $f_i:X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ is integral, so by Morphisms, Lemma 01WM [pqf-lem-integral-univclosed], direction (1)$\Rightarrow$(2), $f_i$ is affine and universally closed. (Source: 'An integral morphism is the same thing as an affine, universally closed morphism. See Morphisms, Lemma [01WM].')

*Step 2 ($f$ is universally closed).* $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ is an fpqc covering of $S$ and, by step 1, every base change $f_i:X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ of $f$ is universally closed. By the descent of universal closedness along fpqc coverings, Descent, Lemma 02KS [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-universally-closed], applied to the same $f$ and the same covering, $f$ is universally closed. (Source: 'combining Lemmas [02KS] and ...'.)

*Step 3 ($f$ is affine).* Likewise, by step 1 every $f_i$ is affine, so by the descent of affineness along fpqc coverings, Descent, Lemma 02L5 [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-affine], applied to $f$ and the covering $\{g_i\}$, $f$ is affine. (Source: '... and [02L5]'.)
*Step 4 ($f$ is integral).* By steps 2 and 3, $f:X\to S$ is affine and universally closed, hence integral by Morphisms, Lemma 01WM [pqf-lem-integral-univclosed], direction (2)$\Rightarrow$(1).
